How I design

Tap or hover a stage to see what I do in it.

AI-first, human-led.

I ask "can AI do this better?" at the start of a task, not as an afterthought. Then I use my own judgement to decide what is actually good for the people using the product.

I'm comfortable using AI tools in my design workflow, for concepts, copy, research synthesis and prototypes. I use generative AI such as ChatGPT to draft, to organise ideas and to find themes in text. Here is how that looks in practice.

AI tools I've usedClaudeChatGPTFigma AICanva AI
01

Explore concepts

At the start of a project I use AI to open up the problem: different angles, questions I haven't asked and directions I could take. I then choose what fits the users and shape it myself.

02

Generate variants

I ask AI for several versions of an idea, such as a flow, a screen's content or a piece of microcopy, so I can compare options side by side and decide faster instead of settling on my first idea.

03

Pressure-test copy

I draft interface text and ask AI to challenge it for clarity, tone and confusing wording. I then rewrite it in my own voice so it still sounds human and fits the product.

04

Synthesise research

I use AI to organise survey answers and interview notes and to find themes in the text. I always check those themes against the original responses before they shape a persona, an empathy map or a design decision.

05

Prototype before specifying

I try to get an idea in front of people early, as a quick prototype, instead of writing a long specification first. AI helps me reach something I can test sooner.

06

Where I stay human

AI gives me speed and options. Judgement stays with me: checking what it produces, using evidence from real users and keeping the work ethical. I'm also strengthening my spreadsheet and data analysis skills so my decisions rest on data.

A little about me.

Mercy WangariUI/UX DesignerKenya

I'm Mercy Wangari, a UI/UX Designer interested in the intersection of people, technology, and design.

I enjoy taking an idea from an early concept and turning it into an experience people can actually understand and use.

My approach is user-centered. I like to understand the problem, explore the people behind it, map their needs, and translate those insights into clear interfaces and meaningful interactions.

I design for people, not just screens.

Every interface has a person on the other side of it.

That's why I believe good UX starts with curiosity. I ask questions, look for patterns, understand frustrations, explore possibilities, and continuously refine the experience.

Make it useful.
Make it simple.
Make it human.
